name: John Howard Adams
personality: Tried to be kind, understanding, generous and demonstrative
notable_stories: Delivered Barbara’s sack lunch to Lowell when he was near Port Townsend on Reserve weekend.
Initially became a 'Catholic of convenience' to simplify marrying a Catholic.
Has maintained a friendship with Kevin Finnegan.
Did not like sharing Barbara with other suitors in Baltimore.
Asked Barbara's father for permission to marry her.
Proposed to Barbara in the basement of her house.
Moved frequently with Barbara during Navy life and later civilian work.
Drove truck for a while after being downsized.
Built a plywood platform over the back seating area for the trip.
Pulled over during Brian's diaper blowout.
Went to Survival School and lost 13 pounds in a week.
Went into the emergency room with Brendan while Barbara waited outside.
Later took Brian to the hospital for his injury.
Reassured Barbara that Brian would be okay.
Provided his own favorite songs list within the artifact.
Blue and Gold admissions officer for USNA
Honeymoon: Drove Annapolis → Pensacola FL for continued flight training
Best Man at wedding: Willie Durkin — John's high school best friend from San Francisco, career SF firefighter, Navy Corpsman at NAS Jacksonville. Died 2021, Alzheimer's complications.

Proposal to Barbara: After the 1968 Army-Navy game, Philadelphia, PA. Conversation-based (no ring, no knee); 'O'Neils, O'Donnels, O'Dells and O'Adams' entourage in hotel room. John subsequently asked Buckey, who replied: 'What makes you think you can support her in the manner she is accustomed on an Ensign's salary in the Navy?' John's starting salary was $345/month plus flight pay.

Engagement ring: 1/2-karat VVS stone bought in Annapolis. Presented to Barbara asleep in the basement of her Baltimore home (Nov 1968). Rating upgraded to 'Flawless' over decades through re-mountings.
Barbara also has a pinky-finger miniature Naval Academy ring with aquamarine stones cut from the same stone as John's Academy ring.
Wedding ring briefly lost playing softball in Port Townsend; replaced by Barbara with a narrower band.
Name origin: John probably after John Kulp (mother's grandfather) or John Wesley Adams (Gen 3). Howard after mother's favorite brother Howard (whose real name was Byron Daniel).
Named 'Howard' after Beryl's favorite brother Byron Daniel 'Howard' Simons (mem).
1952: First big trip — to Okinawa with family.
1954: First family television set; first family car was a used 1949 DeSoto, kept until 1959 departure for Germany.
1964: San Francisco City High School football championship — his school won.
1967 summer: Began courtship of Barbara McKeldin.
1976: Left active duty, joined Navy Reserves as XO, Aviation Maintenance Division, NAS Whidbey Island.
1978: Transitioned to civilian paper industry (engineering, project management, logistics).
1980: Father George Francis Adams Sr. died.
1995: Left Crown (Crown Zellerbach / Crown Pacific); moved to Redding, CA.

NOTE: This source again reports Beryl's death as 1999 (memoir ~p.136: 'would have turned 80 that Christmas Day'). User has previously confirmed 1998-08-01 as correct canonical date — maintaining 1998. Both memoir sources (this + Adams_Direct_Line) report 1999.
2009: Retired at age 62.
Present (2026): Lives between Ridgefield WA and Englewood CO.
Navy call sign: 'Quincy' — but not routinely used as a nickname.

Mid-air collision off USS Ranger: A-6 Intruder struck by F-4 Phantom wingman whose squadron commander had crossed through the carrier's landing pattern. Cockpit fire; aircraft tumbled. John ejected, failed to release parachute on water entry, pulled underwater twice, finally activated strobe light on helmet, picked up within a minute. Bombardier also ejected — cracked neck, more severely burned. (Memoir p.99-102.)
First boss in civilian world: Lowell Tiller, a consummate Mechanical Engineer; Lowell died early from MS. His wife Lillian and Barbara are close friends to this day.
On August 14, 2021, met a 60-year-old cousin for the very first time.
Applied to all service academies; originally received West Point appointment but requested Annapolis as first choice. Father (in South Korea) was somewhat surprised.
Father's advice staying at USNA: 'Well, if you do that, what do you think you'll do with yourself?' — kept John from leaving halfway through Plebe Year.

Career: State of New Mexico school construction financing in Crownpoint, NM. Position came through son Brendan, who was working for Gerald Martin General Contractor and introduced a State of New Mexico representative to John — John was hired as construction manager for public schools in the north-central part of the state.
